nodes.label: Methodology
nodes.question: What methodological approach does the study use to analyze waste re-utilization economies?
nodes.answer: The study offers a comparative analysis using load capacity factors as an alternative proxy to demonstrate the shape of the load capacity curve (LCC) in specified economies.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Waste management|Circular economy practices in waste management_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What aspects of sustainability does the study explore concerning waste management practices?
nodes.answer: The study explores waste management practices informed by local knowledge that support ecological system sustainability.
nodes.subtopic: Circular economy practices in waste management

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Waste management|Circular economy practices in waste management_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Why is finding more sustainable waste management practices considered crucial?
nodes.answer: It is crucial because current methods threaten key sectors such as tourism and occupy valuable land that could otherwise be used for other purposes.
nodes.subtopic: Circular economy practices in waste management

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Waste management|Circular economy practices in waste management_qna_003
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Why was Lagos State selected for the research on SMEs and circular economy practices?
nodes.answer: Lagos State was selected because it is the most populous city in Nigeria and is currently facing challenges with its waste management systems, making it a relevant location for exploring the experiences and challenges of SMEs in implementing circular economy practices.
nodes.subtopic: Circular economy practices in waste management

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Waste management|Circular economy practices in waste management_qna_004
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What challenges are faced by SMEs in Nigeria regarding the implementation of circular economy and environmental sustainability practices?
nodes.answer: SMEs in Nigeria face challenges such as a lack of knowledge and skills, inadequate waste management systems, and difficulties in adopting effective environmental sustainability and circular economic activities.
